label: copy-phase input 3 (also o, i), mostly late in long sequences; very sparse
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (0.0075% of steps). 97% of mass is in the copy phase, where the fed-back input token is 3 (69% of mass), o (16%) or i (11%). It is concentrated at the last two copy steps (to_go <= 1) of long sequences (L = 9 gives 72% of mass, L = 8 gives 16%), i.e. recall_idx 6-8. The strongest activations (up to 0.255) are on input 3 at the end of L=8/9 sequences. It essentially never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, and not on other input tokens. Precision is very poor: copy-phase 3/o/i at recall_idx >= 6 fires under 1% of the time. The previous input (e, g, o, t) raises the rate about 10x, but no simple predicate separates active from inactive cases, so the trigger looks like a specific hidden-state configuration rather than a token rule.
